disagreements.case: B7 B7-76 timeout ends background and new-session children before returning
disagreements.contract: The command and its background/new-session children terminate before cleanup returns; no later write occurs.
disagreements.observed: Full-run timeout cleanup returned; PID 302195 was non-zombie according to the immediate /proc probe. Its command line was already empty in the following receipt. The case failed before reaching its release-marker assertion.
disagreements.classification: Unresolved termination-proof failure, not an established post-cleanup file write. A previous 4/4 focused run and a fresh unchanged 1/1 timeout rerun passed. Full stat bytes were added to subsequent receipts without changing the assertion.
disagreements.cause: Not established. The final failing receipt does not contain the stat snapshot, so it cannot distinguish all kernel exit phases. No timing tolerance, sleep, retry or weaker assertion was added.
disagreements.focused_diagnostic_rerun: test-results/trial7-tests2-lifetime-diagnostics.txt: 4/4, exit 0; unchanged assertions with raw stat receipts

disagreements.case: B7 B7-80 exact 1 MiB shell request reaches Bash with bounded individual argv
disagreements.contract: The shell protocol permits a 1 MiB request; stdin uses subsequent frames of at most 8192 bytes. EOF is a separate 8-byte frame.
disagreements.observed: 1,048,576 request bytes alone: status 0, stdout accepted. Same request plus 8-byte EOF: status 70, empty stdout, stderr whygraph shell launcher unavailable: request too large\n.
disagreements.cause: startClosedShell checks the whole buffered input length before consuming the request, so a coalesced stdin frame counts against the request limit.

contract_silence: Batch 5 describes successive invalid and timeout retry ladders but does not enumerate mixed timeout/breach/harness pairs or all stop diagnostics. The matrix composes those recorded ladders. Batch 7 README and ADR 0011 explicitly preserve their possible third launch.
Batch 5 does not specify crash reservations or a persistent attempt budget. Batch 7 explicitly owns those rules; tests do not impose them on earlier batches.
Relative workRoot and Unix socket path bounds are not specified. Existing short relative aliases keep real sockets within host limits. Functional fixtures initialize their own Git roots.
Smoke ledger schema is not documented. Existing smoke fixtures retain their command-accepted representation; new loop cases use the public applying API.
B7-34 shorthand formula omits a per-list minimum. Existing cases follow ADR 0012 and remain unchanged.

B7-76 does not define a host-PID observation for intermediate kernel exit phases. The final failed child had empty cmdline, but the receipt lacked raw stat bytes. The strict non-zombie assertion stays unchanged while this is diagnosed.
